source_evidence_basis: Prior V3 full-SRT analyses and 2026-10-30 source-limited V4 rechecks; no new original audio/video performed.
model_boundary: All five calculations are explicitly synthetic, educational L2, and must not be treated as personal advice or empirical probabilities.

new_closure_cases.question: Does the timing of a large loss change withdrawal sustainability even with the same annual return multiset?
new_closure_cases.method: For each year: first subtract KRW48m from positive remaining balance, then multiply by 1+that year's return. If start balance < draw, mark that year as exhaustion. No borrowing or tax computation.
limits: Different order of identical yearly returns creates different cashflows when funds are withdrawn.
Yearly withdrawal differs from historic M01 monthly withdrawals and must not be presented as a correction of that model.
Actual asset allocation, pension taxes, inflation, health expenses, volatility and personal withdrawals not verified.
new_closure_cases.decision_cap: L2 hypothetical only; no withdrawal rate recommendation

new_closure_cases.question: For one year, what is the simple interest avoided by fully reducing a hypothetical high-interest debt versus investing the same principal?
new_closure_cases.method: Debt avoided = principal * loan APR; investing net gain = principal * gross return * (1 - gain tax proxy). Flat principal, no amortization, capital-loss risk or tax deductibility.
limits: 12% debt is a fictional loan rate, not a current contract quote; loan fees, prepayment penalties and amortization ignored.
15.4% is a scenario gain-tax proxy, not an assertion that every ETF, ISA or pension gain bears this rate.
Employer match, account tax advantages, liquidity and emergency savings may change priority.
new_closure_cases.decision_cap: L2 conditional arithmetic only; no automatic debt repayment order

new_closure_cases.question: How do applicable deferred retirement income tax fractions vary with actual pension receipt year from 2026-01-01?
new_closure_cases.method: Apply 70% (receipt years 1-10), 60% (11-20), or 50% (>20) to a fixed hypothetical tax assessment of the same eligible deferred-retirement-income amount. Not a forecast of a total account's taxes.
limits: Actual receipt year is not automatically established by merely submitting a nominal KRW10,000 start request.

Do not use aggregate year counts as a statement of tax due on unchanged whole withdrawal; actual payment-specific deferred tax allocation, minimum age, withdrawal limits and account records are required.
Rules verified as of research date; effective 2026-01-01 per NTS, tax law changes require recheck.
new_closure_cases.decision_cap: L2 eligible tax-fraction demonstration; personal IRP start blocked

new_closure_cases.question: What one-year gain is needed to justify holding a loss-making equity versus switching into a hypothetical alternative, ignoring the historical cost basis?
new_closure_cases.method: Hold=present value*(1+old future return). Replace=present value*(1-switch cost)*(1+alternative future return). Break-even hold return=(1-fee)*(1+alternative return)-1; past cost is sunk for future return comparison.
limits: None of the assumed future returns are forecasts, and replacement is not universally preferable.
Cost basis still matters for actual capital-gains tax, tax loss harvesting, diversification, dividend policy, market liquidity and legal constraints.
Issuer fundamentals and actual ticker remain unavailable, so no L3 ranking.

new_closure_cases.question: How long would a fictional new employee take to build a 3- or 6-month minimum expense reserve before adding locked-up investment commitments?
new_closure_cases.method: Target = (essential expenses + debt payments)*number of months; time to target = ceiling((target-initial reserve)/monthly emergency contribution); check cash-flow feasibility against take-home pay.
limits: Three to six months is a scenario planning range, not a mandated reserve for every investor.
No reserve interest/inflation, existing savings, irregular income, employer benefits or new emergency events modeled.
Specific youth savings product, ISA pension tax preference and actual salary/debt remain unverified.

note: Appends five independently testable scenarios without changing prior 9 model results or 62 V3 claim identifiers.
